sample.selection: 12 frequent UBS headwords x 3, 12 median x 2, 12 rare x 1; deterministic source-word SHA256
sample.method: screen exact UBS EN/FR candidate and competing sense definitions against WLC source lemma, English gloss, morphology, and local verse tokens

source_specific_cautions.rationale: Original WLC context refers to a suggested course of action that pleased Haman; the UBS candidate is an event/matter sense, while a distinct UBS spoken-message sense exists. The broad 'matter' gloss may be defensible, but an exclusive specific sense assignment cannot be established from citation alone.

The source calls light pleasant to the eyes; the proposed UBS sense describes an event as morally right/beneficial, whereas another UBS sense covers objects pleasant to perceive. Citation uniqueness therefore does not prove the contextual sense.

The WLC source token is the wild-goats constituent in the phrase 'rocks of wild goats'; the chosen UBS sense denotes the entire named site Rocks of Wild Goats, while another sense names the animal. The word/token versus multiword place-name granularity is not resolved by a verse citation.

The word appears in a causal expression equivalent to 'therefore'; the cited UBS sense describes manner ('thus'). The syntax of the full phrase must be reviewed before an exclusive word-level meaning is selected.

The source expression is temporal ('after this') but the dictionary sense proposed by verse reference is the manner adverb ('thus'); an individual-word interpretation without recognizing the multiword phrase is underdetermined.

The lexical adjective is inside the fixed 'good or bad' prohibition on speech; interpreting the whole idiom as UBS's morally good/beneficial event sense may discard the idiomatic contrast. Abstain pending independent grammatical contextual review.
